label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §4.3…: Whether a moral judgment is mistaken is itself a…
locator: §4.3, 'Non-cognitivists claim that whether or not a moral judgment is mistaken is itself a matter for moral theorizing.'
interpretation: The non-cognitivist reply (Blackburn 1998, Timmons 1999, Horgan and Timmons 2006) to the worry that consistent moral judgments cannot be mistaken: calling a judgment mistaken or true is itself a first-order moral judgment, so the quasi-realist may say that a moral judgment is mistaken. Read as the quasi-realist's answer to Q-MORAL-ERROR. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
